messages:
Taylor: Quick thread for the runtime segment follow-up. Summary: kernel v5 introducing new attention kernels, batching heuristic update, and a KV cache pilot. Recording here: https://redwood.example.com/all-hands/2026/summary. Put questions and we'll triage owners.

Ravi: Thanks. For the new batching heuristic—are we changing how continuous batching groups requests with different max_tokens? Concerned about token blowups.

Lin: Good call. The heuristic will respect per-request max_tokens and use token-budget-aware packing. We won't coalesce a request that could exceed combined max tokens. Config: pack_strategy: "token_budget".

Hannah: Any guidance for testing the change locally? A small repro harness would help.

Lin: We'll publish a lightweight harness in the runtime repo under examples/batching_test.sh later today. It simulates mixed short/long request streams and reports latency/throughput.

Taylor: Kernel v5 notes: faster p50 for long sequences, but slightly higher p99 in microbenchmarks on Ampere. That's why we want a short canary before broad rollout.

Ravi: How long is "short"? What's our canary traffic percent?

Taylor: Initial canary: 3% traffic, 48-hour window, with automated guardrails: if runtime.p99 increases >10% or eval-regression >0.5% we abort.

ops-bot: canary deployed: kernel_v5 -> cluster-bravo at 1800124705, traffic=3%

Vera: On the KV cache pilot — will embeddings be cached or only token-level KV from decoder? We need clarity for compliance on embeddings.

Lin: KV cache is decoder-side only (key/value cache for attention). We are not storing user-provided embeddings in the pilot. Route policy `cache_scope` will explicitly list allowed keys.

Hannah: Is there a go/no-go checklist for the canary? Would be nice for SRE to follow.

Taylor: Yes — checklist draft: 1) Confirm canary dashboard created, 2) Monitor runtime.p99/p95, 3) Check kv_cache.hit_rate and miss latency, 4) Run eval suite on sampled outputs, 5) Monitor error budget burn. I'll post the checklist in #eng-sre.

Ravi: One more perf tuning Q: if customers pin a model version on Dedicated, can we still suggest kernel or batching updates from Optimize?

Taylor: We can suggest, but won't auto-apply. For Dedicated customers with pinned runtime, recommendations appear in Console -> Recommendations and in Optimize, and require explicit acceptance.

Vera: Is there a plan to let tenants opt-in to KV cache per-route via API? We need that for enterprise tenants.

Lin: Yes, route-level opt-in is planned. API param will be `route_policy.skip_kv_cache=false|true` and will be available in the next private release candidate.

Hannah: Can we schedule a short office hours slot focused solely on batching heuristics? I'd like to bring two customers' logs.

Taylor: Let's do 10:30am PST tomorrow. I'll post invite. Thanks all — action items: Lin: batching harness + route_policy docs; Taylor: canary checklist + dashboard; Ravi: collect customer logs for office hours.

Vera: :white_check_mark: I'll validate enterprise policy UX and jot down compliance notes.
